script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Family
Theme: second chances

Begin screenplay.

---

INT. KITCHEN - MORNING

JANE (35, determined, single mother) stands at the kitchen counter, preparing breakfast. Her three children, AIDEN (11), SAM (8), and EMMA (6), sit at the table, chattering excitedly.

AIDEN
Mom, can we have cereal today?

JANE
(smiling)
Sure, sweetie. I'll make pancakes instead.

Suddenly, the doorbell rings. Jane glances at the clock. It's not even 9:00 a.m.

JANE
(to herself)
That can't be good.

INT. ENTRANCEWAY - CONTINUOUS

Jane opens the door to reveal her ex-husband, MARK (40, disheveled, regretting). He carries a small bag of groceries.

MARK
Hi, Jane. I brought some things.

JANE
(nervously)
Mark, what are you doing here?

MARK
(awkwardly)
I just wanted to talk. I've been thinking about our marriage... and I realize I made a mistake. I want a second chance.

Jane hesitates, then steps aside to let him in. The children notice and stare, wide-eyed.

INT. LIVING ROOM - LATER

Mark and Jane sit on the couch, facing each other. The children play in the background.

MARK
I know I hurt you, Jane. I was selfish and didn't appreciate what we had. I want to make it up to you and the kids.

JANE
(sighs)
Mark, I don't know if this is a good idea. We both made mistakes.

MARK
(pleading)
Please, Jane. I've changed. I've been going to therapy and I've been trying to be a better person. I want us to be a family again.

JANE
(skeptical)
I need time to think about this.

INT. KITCHEN - EVENING

Jane is alone in the kitchen, looking at the children's drawings on the refrigerator. Mark enters, carrying a takeout bag.

MARK
I brought dinner. I know you've been busy.

JANE
(surprised)
Thank you.

Mark sets the table and helps Jane serve the food. They sit down to eat in silence.

INT. LIVING ROOM - NIGHT

Jane, Mark, and the children watch a movie together on the couch. The kids snuggle up between them, and they all laugh at the jokes.

MARK
(whispering to Jane)
I'm really glad we're doing this. I want to be a good husband and a good father.

JANE
(smiling)
I want that too. But we have to take it one day at a time.

INT. JANE'S BEDROOM - NIGHT

Jane lies in bed, thinking. She hears Mark's gentle breathing from the other room. She turns over and closes her eyes, a small smile on her lips.

INT. KITCHEN - MORNING

The sun rises as Jane stands at the kitchen counter, preparing breakfast. Mark enters, carrying the newspaper.

MARK
Good morning, beautiful.

JANE
(smiling)
Good morning.

They share a tender moment before the chaos of the day begins. The children enter, and the family goes about their day, united and ready for a fresh start.

FADE OUT.

---

End of screenplay.
